description: Atomically apply an array of CompositionOps to a project composition. All ops succeed or none do (transactional). Call describe_composition_ops without type for the compact operation list, then with a type for its exact JSON Schema. For negotiated component execution, read get_composition with componentExecutionVersions=["3","4"] and includeDependencies="true", then send componentExecutionVersions:[3,4] and that exact expectedBrandIdentity. A changed brand refuses the command; never refresh the witness to conceal a conflict. Explicit builtinSources selectors attach only the approved exact source pins referenced by the final composition. The additive `concurrency` envelope requires an endpoint confirmed to enforce guardedCompositionV1; unsupported hosted endpoints refuse it with unsupported_concurrency. Obtain dependency expectations from the observed composition; never rebuild a stale basis from current state. Every committing call REQUIRES `if_match`, the composition ETag from a fresh get_composition, or the `concurrency` envelope; a call with neither is refused with 428 precondition_required. On 409 stale_etag, read get_composition again and reconsider the batch against what changed; never copy the error's currentEtag into a retry without that read. `dry_run: true` validates without persisting. For negotiated component execution, EVERY dry-run and commit must still carry the observed `composition_id`, `concurrency:{mode:"exact",expectedRevision:<observed project revision>}` (or supported guarded dependency expectations), `componentExecutionVersions` and exact `expectedBrandIdentity`; retain the observed `if_match` too. Only non-negotiated legacy dry-runs may omit revision preconditions. Ops land on the project's ACTIVE composition unless you pass `composition_id` (mutually exclusive with `session_id`), which targets a specific one — that is how you author a second composition minted with new_composition and run an A/B. Use this to seed a composition (add media clips) or make targeted edits (set a crop intent, reorder clips, set the format). CAPTIONS FOR EDITED TIMELINES: after saving all clip edits, call again with {type:"captions.fromComposition", trackId} to build captions from every audible clip on that track, honoring trims, exclusions and placement. Clips must have duration matching playable source duration divided by playbackRate; unsupported timing fails explicitly. Re-run it after later timeline edits; captions do not update automatically. {type:"captions.fromTranscript", mediaId, window?} instead replaces all captions from one media transcript, rebased to zero; it does not follow a montage. Style with {type:"setCaptionStyle", style}; or set explicit words with {type:"setCaptions", segments, style?} (e.g. translations or your own VO timings). Brand is NOT set here — it lives on the project (create_project / update_project with brandKitId — or PATCH /projects/:id over REST). CARDS: a {kind:"card", html, tokens} clip projects each `tokens` KEY `x` to the CSS custom property `--cf-x`, so the html must read it as `var(--cf-x)` — write `tokens:{"plate":"#0af"}` + `background:var(--cf-plate)`. Do NOT put dashes in the key: `"--plate"` becomes `--cf---plate` and your `var(--plate)` then resolves to NOTHING, which CSS silently degrades to a transparent background and black text. Responses carry `warnings[]` when a card reads a var nothing defines. SCENE SHOTS: for a 3D product shot — a tilted page screenshot, a lit laptop/phone showing a real screenshot, two-colour type, a colour-field backdrop, focus/grain/vignette and a camera move — use {type:"scene.add", clipId, newTrack|trackId, startTime, duration, scene, assets} and revise it with {type:"scene.update", clipId, scene?, assets?, startTime?, duration?}. You author a scene SPEC, never wrapper TSX; the server registers the component for you. There is NO built-in scene primitive in list_catalog — READ cueframe://scene-shot first for the JSON schema, the canonical V2 world-objects recipe with nested groups, slabs, pages, phones, laptops, world/screen text, admitted surfaces, camera motion, lighting, and the current resource limits.

__schema307.description: Version 1 shared dependency admission. Guarded requests must name the observed immutable composition with composition_id or concurrency.compositionId; changed or missing dependencies refuse the entire batch.

__schema311.description: OCC precondition: the strong etag (`"<hex>"`) the caller last saw. Required unless `concurrency` is sent or `dry_run` is true; a write with neither is refused with 428 precondition_required. On mismatch the batch is rejected (409 stale_etag) before any op applies.

__schema312.description: When true, validate the batch (apply + projection accept/reject guards) WITHOUT persisting. Returns `{ valid, errors }` instead of applying.

__schema313.description: Target a SPECIFIC composition instead of the project's active one. Omit it and the project's active composition is edited, which is the default and the common case. `preview_frame` and `create_render` already accept a compositionId; this closes the gap so a second composition minted with `new_composition` can actually be authored into — build variant A, mint B, edit B, preview both. Mutually exclusive with `session_id`, which targets the session's scratch.

__schema314.description: Optional compose-session id. When present, the ops target the session's SCRATCH composition (a derived sibling) instead of the project's active composition — the server never mutates active until commit.

body.description: POST /projects/:id/composition/apply body — a batch of CompositionOps.

ops.description: Call describe_composition_ops for the operation list, then with a type for its exact JSON Schema.

commandId.description: Retry identity. A call repeated with the same commandId returns the first result instead of acting twice.

response.description: MCP response view. Default compact omits repeated source bodies. Full returns the complete backend receipt or requested sources. This does not change the saved composition.

name: apply_composition

anyOf.description: Verbatim backend JSON object, or an explicitly identified full selected-clip view.
